stories.title: Why Japan’s anti-hate measures fall short
stories.summary: Anti-immigration policy protest in Oct 2026. Screen capture from the Japan Unfiltered YouTube Channel. Fair Use This post is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “ Justice as infrastructure .” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law ( HiiL ) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here . A newborn Black baby delivered at a clinic in Tokyo’s Meguro Ward became the target of a barrage of racist harassment online. The clinic published the baby’s photo with a congratulatory message on its social media account as part of its routine “babies born this month” photo series. A screenshot of the post spread widely on X, gaining more than 1.3 million views within a day. The post attracted many hateful comments loaded with anti-immigrant sentiment and racial discrimination against non-white and non-Japanese people.

stories.title: Major boost to local housing and regeneration ambitions as regional leaders strengthen co-delivery ties with Homes England and National Housing Bank
stories.summary: Mayors and leaders central to new wave of Place Delivery Agreements that back local priorities through joint commitments, resources and expertise. Mayors, regional leaders, Homes England and the National Housing Bank have agreed multiple ground-breaking collaborations in the last two months that will accelerate co-delivery of local housing and regeneration plans across England. This includes the first wave of new Place Delivery Agreements (PDAs) , first outlined by the housing minister in September, which give mayors a stronger role in shaping housing delivery, regeneration and growth. Individual agreements with South Yorkshire Combined Mayoral Authority, East Midlands Combined County Authority, West Midlands Combined Mayoral Authority, North East Mayoral Combined Authority, West of England Combined Authority and Liverpool City Region Combined Authority have now been published, with more partnerships to be announced shortly.

stories.title: Member reappointed to the Treasure Valuation Committee
stories.summary: The Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport has reappointed Professor Leslie Webster as a Member of the Treasure Valuation Committee for a five-year term. Appointed from 15 April 2027 to 14 April 2032 Professor Webster is a specialist in early medieval art and archaeology. She was formerly a senior curator of the British Museum’s Anglo-Saxon, late Celtic and Viking collections and Keeper of the Department of Britain, Europe and Prehistory. She has served as an Honorary Visiting Professor at the Institute of Archaeology, University College London, and as President of the Society for Medieval Archaeology and is a Fellow of the Society of Antiquaries. She has lectured and published widely. Her recent books include Anglo-Saxon Art: A New History (2012), The Franks Casket (2012), and, as co-editor and contributor, The Staffordshire Hoard: an Anglo-Saxon Treasure (2019). Members of the Treasure Valuation Committee are not remunerated.

stories.title: The Stormy Southwest Pacific
stories.summary: Tropical Cyclone Xavier launched the basin’s storm season with a bang. Even as the unusually quiet 2026 storm season winds down in the North Atlantic, seas have begun to stir on the other side of the world in the Southwest Pacific. On November 15, 2026 , the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier , the system intensified rapidly , thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones . Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati , a short-lived storm that emerged in October.
stories.why_it_matters: Science news is a chance to ask what the evidence shows and what is still being studied.
